beats.say: Pull request {{facts.number}}, by {{facts.authorLogin}}: authenticating to a locked Private Marketplace. {{facts.additions}} lines added across {{facts.changedFiles}} files. Still open for review.

claims.text: PR number, author, additions, changed files, state are as GitHub reports

beats.say: A Private Marketplace can demand a token minted for the marketplace itself. A sign-in token only says who you are. And the marketplace's identity can't live in product.json, because every company registers its own.

claims.text: a Private Marketplace with authentication enforced refuses its service index unless it gets a token minted for the marketplace itself; the sign-in token identifies the user but its audience is not the marketplace
the marketplace's resource identity can't be shipped in product.json because a self-hosted deployment has its own app registration

beats.say: So VS Code asks at runtime, using RFC 9728. One: request the index. Two: on a 401 or 403, read the marketplace's well-known metadata for its authorization server and scopes. Three: get a token scoped to that resource. Four: retry. If step one works, nothing else runs.

claims.text: the service index is first read with the bearer the account already carries
a 401 or 403 from the service index is treated as 'authentication required' (MarketplaceAuthRequiredError)
discoverProtectedResource reads the marketplace's protected resource metadata and returns its first authorization server and its supported scopes
a resource-scoped token is requested from the account service via getAccount(protectedResource) and the index is read again with it
if the first request succeeds no discovery or negotiation happens

beats.say: Then the careful part: where the token may go. getAuthorizationHeaders sends it only over https, to exactly the service index's origin. Public-marketplace downloads stay anonymous, and a shared parent domain doesn't count.

claims.text: the bearer is attached only to https requests whose authority equals the service index's authority, and fails closed otherwise
upstreamed extensions are fetched from the public Microsoft marketplace and must not receive the private marketplace's token
parent-domain matching is deliberately not used because a marketplace can share its parent domain with unrelated tenants

beats.say: The same bearer covers search, downloads, and extension resources like icons and README. It also travels over IPC to the shared process and, when connected, the remote server. If access is still refused, users now get RequiresSignIn, not a dead-end AccessDenied.

claims.text: the bearer is attached to search (extensionquery), control manifest, asset/VSIX downloads and extension resource requests (icons, README, CHANGELOG)
the token and the index origin are pushed over the extensionGalleryManifest channel to the shared process and, when there is one, the remote server
a marketplace that still requires authentication after negotiation now reports RequiresSignIn instead of AccessDenied
